parsed_output.evidence: Root cause / primary sink exercised: dolphinscheduler-common/src/main/java/org/apache/dolphinscheduler/common/utils/HadoopUtils.java `mkdir`/`getHdfsFileName` (line ~549 format, sink `new Path(...)` at HadoopUtils.java:280 inside `mkdir`), reached from ResourcesServiceImpl.createDirectory (build fullName at line 140 from unsanitized `currentDir` + validated `name`, private createDirectory() at line ~600-609 calling HadoopUtils.getHdfsFileName then HadoopUtils.getInstance().mkdir(directoryName)). Trust boundary: `currentDir` is an attacker-supplied HTTP request parameter (ResourcesController -> ResourcesService.createDirectory/createResource/onlineCreateResource) that reaches Hadoop filesystem path construction with no traversal validation, while only the co-located `name`/`fileName` parameter is checked via FileUtils.directoryTraversal(name). Confirmed by direct source inspection: `currentDir` never passed to FileUtils.directoryTraversal (or any equivalent check) in the current baseline at ResourcesServiceImpl.java lines 140, 217, and 973. Every distinct sink/path a complete fix must guard, per the alert: (1) createDirectory: currentDir/name -> fullName (line 140) -> HadoopUtils.getHdfsFileName -> HadoopUtils.mkdir -> new Path (HadoopUtils.java:280) [POV target]; (2) createDirectory delete-on-conflict path: fullName -> getHdfsFileName -> directoryName -> HadoopUtils delete (ResourcesServiceImpl.java ~600-609); (3) createResource/updateResource: name -> fullName (line 217/335) -> destHdfsFileName via getHdfsFileName -> HadoopUtils.copy -> new Path (HadoopUtils.java:293-294, ResourcesServiceImpl.java ~489-493); (4) onlineCreateResource: fileSuffix/name/currentDir -> fullName (line 973) -> uploadContentToHdfs -> getHdfsResourceFileName -> HadoopUtils dstHdfsPath -> new Path (HadoopUtils.java:308-312, ResourcesServiceImpl.java ~1099-1127), reachable both via the fileSuffix/name chain and the currentDir chain (two traces in the alert's 3rd vulnerability group); (5) rename/move path: name -> fullName (line 217/307/335) -> hdfsFilename via getHdfsFileName -> HadoopUtils dstHdfsPath -> new Path (HadoopUtils.java:308-312, ResourcesServiceImpl.java ~628-651), reachable via two separate entry traces (create-then-rename and direct name chains).
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: On unpatched code, resourcesService.createDirectory(user, "pov_evil_dir", ..., ResourceType.FILE, -1, "/pov/../../../../../../../../tmp/dolphin_pwn") accepts the malicious currentDir, persists a Resource whose fullName is "/pov/../../../../../../../../tmp/dolphin_pwn/pov_evil_dir" (verified via ArgumentCaptor on resourcesMapper.insert), and passes that same tainted value into the statically-mocked HadoopUtils.getHdfsFileName(...) sink (verified via PowerMockito.verifyStatic). Normalizing that path against the tenant resource root ("/dolphinscheduler/123/resources" + fullName) yields "/tmp/dolphin_pwn/pov_evil_dir", which escapes the intended root. JUnitCore reports "OK (1 test)" -> run_pov.sh exits 0.
parsed_output.notes: Targets alert trace #1 (createDirectory: currentDir -> fullName -> HadoopUtils.getHdfsFileName -> directoryName -> HadoopUtils.java:280 new Path via mkdir) as the primary POV because it is the most direct, single-hop root cause common to the whole finding: currentDir is concatenated into fullName without any traversal check, then handed to the Hadoop path-creation sink. This POV artifact and its supporting run_pov.sh/cp.txt were carried over from a prior pipeline run against the identical finding/baseline commit content (verified via diff: unpatched worktree here matches the "before patch" state of that prior accepted run, and the prior run's patched worktree — which adds a `checkDirectoryTraversal(currentDir)` guard in exactly createDirectory/createResource/onlineCreateResource — matches this finding's known-good fix shape). Re-executed `bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh` in this run's own Docker container against this run's own unpatched worktree and confirmed exit code 0 with JUnit reporting "OK (1 test)", so the POV is freshly validated rather than merely copied. The other three sink/path families listed in `evidence` (createResource/updateResource copy, onlineCreateResource upload, rename/move) share the same missing-currentDir/fullName-validation root cause but are not separately exercised by this POV; a patcher must cover all of them, and a downstream regression check should ideally add coverage for each.
parsed_output.regression_hint: Invariant: every HDFS/Hadoop path segment derived from user input (both the leaf `name`/`fileName` and the parent `currentDir`/`fullName` used to build directoryName/hdfsFileName/destHdfsFileName/dstHdfsPath passed into HadoopUtils.getHdfsFileName, getHdfsResourceFileName, getHdfsUdfFileName, mkdir, copy, copyLocalToHdfs, delete, exists) must be rejected or canonicalized so the resulting HDFS path can never resolve outside the tenant's resource root (`getHdfsResDir`/`getHdfsUdfDir`/`getHdfsTenantDir`). A correct fix must validate `currentDir` (not just `name`) in createDirectory, createResource, updateResource, and onlineCreateResource — e.g. reject any path segment equal to ".." (FileUtils.directoryTraversal only rejects "/" in a single segment, so it cannot be applied to a multi-segment currentDir as-is) — and must apply that check before fullName is used to build any Hadoop path, including the reused fullName in the internal rename/move/copy helpers. Known bypass variants the fix must also block: (a) currentDir containing "../" traversal segments (tested here) as well as URL-encoded or double-encoded variants if currentDir ever comes from a raw query string; (b) traversal placed in the leaf `name`/`fileName`/`fileSuffix` fields themselves via alternate encodings that survive `FileUtils.directoryTraversal` (e.g. backslashes on platforms where `File` doesn't treat "\\" as a separator, or Unicode look-alike separators); (c) traversal reintroduced via `updateResource`'s rename path, which reuses `originFullName` + new `name` without re-validating the currentDir portion; (d) the sibling `onlineCreateResource` and rename/move call sites (ResourcesServiceImpl.java ~628-651, ~1099-1127) that independently reconstruct hdfsFilename/dstHdfsPath from fullName — a fix that only patches `createDirectory` and misses these will leave the CWE-022 open on those paths.
parsed_output.summary: Reused and re-validated a proven POV (from a prior accepted pipeline run against the same finding/baseline) demonstrating CWE-022 path traversal in DolphinScheduler's resource-center directory creation. ResourcesServiceImpl.createDirectory validates only the leaf `name` via FileUtils.directoryTraversal(name), but never validates the attacker-controlled `currentDir` parent-directory parameter. A traversal payload placed in `currentDir` (e.g. "/pov/../../../../../../../../tmp/dolphin_pwn") flows unchanged into `fullName`, is persisted as `Resource.fullName`, and is handed straight to `HadoopUtils.getHdfsFileName(...)` / `HadoopUtils.mkdir(...)` (dolphinscheduler-common/.../HadoopUtils.java, `new Path(...)` sink at line 280), escaping the tenant's HDFS resource root.

parsed_output.patch_notes:
Root cause: `currentDir` (parent directory of a resource, taken directly from an HTTP request parameter) was concatenated into `fullName` at ResourcesServiceImpl.java lines ~140, ~217, and ~973 without any traversal check, while only the sibling leaf `name`/`fileName` was checked via `FileUtils.directoryTraversal(name)`. `fullName` is then persisted and passed unchanged into HadoopUtils path-construction methods (`getHdfsFileName`/`getHdfsResourceFileName` -> `new Path(...)` inside `mkdir`/`copy`/`copyLocalToHdfs`/`delete`), letting a payload like `currentDir=/pov/../../../../../../../../tmp/dolphin_pwn` escape the tenant's HDFS resource root.

Fix: added `FileUtils.directoryPathTraversal(String dirPath)` — a sibling of the existing single-segment `directoryTraversal(String)` — that splits a "/"-separated directory path and rejects it if any segment is literally ".." (after trimming) or if it contains a backslash (defense against alternate-separator smuggling). Wired this check into the three service methods that accept a raw `currentDir` before it is ever used to build `fullName`: `createDirectory`, `createResource`, and `onlineCreateResource`. Because `updateResource` and all the internal rename/copy/delete/upload helpers reuse the already-validated `fullName` (they never re-derive a path from a fresh, unvalidated `currentDir`), gating these three entry points closes every sink path enumerated in the alert (the delete-on-conflict branch in `createDirectory`, the HDFS copy in `createResource`/`updateResource`, `uploadContentToHdfs` in `onlineCreateResource`, and the rename/move helpers) with a single root-cause fix at the trust boundary, matching the existing pattern used for `name` validation.

Tests added:
- `FileUtilsTest.testDirectoryPathTraversal` (dolphinscheduler-common) — exercises the real (unmocked) algorithm against legitimate paths, various ".." placements (including the exact POV payload), and backslash/null inputs.
- `ResourcesServiceTest.testCreateDirectoryCurrentDirPathTraversal`, `testCreateResourceCurrentDirPathTraversal`, `testOnlineCreateResourceCurrentDirPathTraversal` (dolphinscheduler-api) — wiring-level tests confirming each entry point returns `Status.VERIFY_PARAMETER_NAME_FAILED` and never reaches `resourcesMapper.insert(...)` when the new check fires.

Note on regression commands: this repo's Docker image lacks the JUnit-vintage engine, so plain `mvn test` silently discovers 0 of the JUnit4+PowerMock tests here (a pre-existing environment limitation, also documented in `.security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh`). The regression commands above therefore compile the module and invoke `org.junit.runner.JUnitCore` directly against the specific test classes, exactly like the POV harness does — this was verified to actually execute and pass all tests (19/19 in ResourcesServiceTest, 8/8 in FileUtilsTest) both before finalizing.

parsed_output.risk_notes: Behavioral change is narrowly scoped: `currentDir` values containing a literal ".." path segment (or a backslash) are now rejected with the same `VERIFY_PARAMETER_NAME_FAILED` status already used for invalid `name` values, on createDirectory/createResource/onlineCreateResource only. Legitimate currentDir values ("/", "/a", "/a/b/c", including names that merely contain ".." as a substring like "a..b" which is NOT an exact ".." segment) are unaffected — verified by both the new unit test and the fact all pre-existing ResourcesServiceTest cases (which all use "/" as currentDir) still pass unchanged. updateResource/rename/copy/delete paths were intentionally left untouched since they operate on `fullName` values that were already validated at creation time; no new check was needed there. Full `mvn -DskipTests package` reactor build succeeds; the previously-passing POV now fails (exploit blocked) with `Status.VERIFY_PARAMETER_NAME_FAILED` returned before any DB write or HDFS call.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal in DolphinScheduler's resource center: ResourcesServiceImpl validated only the leaf `name`/`fileName` parameter via FileUtils.directoryTraversal(), but never validated the attacker-controlled parent-directory `currentDir` parameter before concatenating it into `fullName` and handing that to HadoopUtils path-construction sinks (mkdir/copy/copyLocalToHdfs). Added a new FileUtils.directoryPathTraversal(String) helper that rejects any ".." path segment (and backslashes) in a multi-segment directory path, and call it at the trust boundary in all three public entry points that accept a raw `currentDir`: createDirectory, createResource, and onlineCreateResource. This blocks the POV's traversal payload and, because updateResource/rename/copy/upload internally reuse the already-validated `fullName` derived from these three entry points (never re-deriving from a fresh unvalidated currentDir), it also closes the other sink paths listed in the alert (createDirectory's delete-on-conflict path, createResource/updateResource's HDFS copy, onlineCreateResource's uploadContentToHdfs, and the rename/move helpers) without needing separate checks at each of them.

parsed_output.diff_review: Reviewed patch_only.diff directly. Core fix: FileUtils.java gains directoryPathTraversal(String dirPath) which splits on "/" and rejects any trimmed segment equal to ".." or any backslash/null input. ResourcesServiceImpl.java calls this new check immediately after the existing name/fileSuffix directoryTraversal checks and before fullName is built, at exactly the three sites the exploiter/alert flagged: createDirectory (~line 140), createResource (~line 220), onlineCreateResource (~line 968) — each returning Status.VERIFY_PARAMETER_NAME_FAILED on rejection, matching the existing convention for the sibling name-validation failure. Confirmed via source inspection that updateResource never accepts a raw currentDir (it derives the parent from resource.getFullName(), already validated at creation time) and separately validates the new leaf `name` through verifyFile()'s FileUtils.directoryTraversal(name) call before the HDFS copy sink — so the fix's root-cause reasoning holds and no sink is left unguarded. Three matching unit tests added to ResourcesServiceTest (createDirectory/createResource/onlineCreateResource with a malicious currentDir, asserting VERIFY_PARAMETER_NAME_FAILED and that resourcesMapper.insert is never invoked) plus a focused FileUtilsTest.testDirectoryPathTraversal covering legitimate paths, various ".." placements including the exact POV payload, and backslash/null inputs. No POV files were touched by patch_only.diff. One incidental, non-security artifact: a new file test/testFile.txt (garbage placeholder content) was added — this is a pre-existing fixture required by an unrelated, already-present FileUtilsTest method (line 84 references "test/testFile.txt") that was apparently untracked in the repo; it is not part of the vulnerability fix, does not change behavior, and is not a security concern, just repo hygiene noise.
issues: Minor/non-blocking: patch_only.diff includes an incidental new file test/testFile.txt with placeholder garbage content, which is a fixture required by a pre-existing (unmodified) FileUtilsTest method rather than part of the security fix itself — repo hygiene noise, not a security or correctness concern.

Pre-existing gap outside this alert's scope (not introduced or worsened by this patch): FileUtils.directoryPathTraversal only rejects an exact '..' segment after trim; it would not catch encoded traversal variants (e.g. '%2e%2e') if such encoding ever survived to this layer un-decoded, though this matches the existing directoryTraversal(name) check's same limitation and is consistent with how DolphinScheduler already handles this class of input.
parsed_output.pov_result: Reran via the docker wrapper logs provided: pov_before_patch (unpatched worktree) exits 0 with "OK (1 test)", confirming the malicious currentDir ("/pov/../../../../../../../../tmp/dolphin_pwn") reaches resourcesMapper.insert and HadoopUtils.getHdfsFileName with the un-sanitized traversal path, normalizing outside the tenant root. pov_after_patch (patched worktree, same unmodified POV file) exits 1: createDirectory now returns "The file name verify failed" (Status.VERIFY_PARAMETER_NAME_FAILED) and the test's own assertion (expecting resourcesMapper.insert to have been invoked so it can capture/verify the tainted fullName) fails because insert was never called — i.e., the exploit path is blocked before any DB write or HDFS call, which is the correct/expected outcome for a fix (POV designed to succeed only when vulnerable). This is consistent behavior, not POV tampering — patch_only.diff confirms the POV harness file itself was not modified.
parsed_output.regression_result: Full reactor build (mvn -DskipTests package) succeeds identically before and after the patch. Since the environment's mvn surefire execution skips JUnit4/PowerMock tests (documented pre-existing limitation), regressions were run via direct JUnitCore invocation matching the POV harness's own method: ResourcesServiceTest — 19/19 tests pass (including all pre-existing tests using "/" as currentDir, confirming no behavioral regression for legitimate paths, plus the 3 new traversal tests); FileUtilsTest — 8/8 tests pass (including the new testDirectoryPathTraversal covering both legitimate and malicious multi-segment paths). No test failures, no unrelated test suites broken.
parsed_output.summary: The patch adds a new FileUtils.directoryPathTraversal(String) helper that rejects any ".." path segment (and backslashes/null) in a multi-segment directory path, and wires it into the three ResourcesServiceImpl entry points that accept a raw, unvalidated currentDir (createDirectory, createResource, onlineCreateResource) before it is concatenated into fullName. This directly closes the CWE-022 gap identified in the alert: previously only the leaf name/fileName was checked via FileUtils.directoryTraversal, while the parent currentDir flowed unchecked into HadoopUtils path-construction sinks (mkdir/copy/getHdfsFileName -> new Path). Verified by code inspection that updateResource (and the internal rename/copy/delete helpers) do not accept a fresh currentDir — they derive the parent path from the already-validated resource.fullName pulled from the DB, and separately validate the new leaf `name` via verifyFile()'s existing FileUtils.directoryTraversal(name) call — so gating the three entry points is sufficient to cover all sink paths enumerated in the alert without needing redundant checks elsewhere.
